what: Which of the darkroom's 68 plates can be authored as engine positives today, and what blocks the rest. Measured from the registry GLSL, not estimated.
why_a_class_and_not_a_backlog: "Port the rest when there is time" hides the fact that most of them cannot be ported at all with the vocabulary that exists. The blocker is one missing construct, and naming it turns fourteen open-ended tasks into one decision.

the_vocabulary_that_exists.sum(n, k => term): a bounded float reduction. Emits a real for-loop with a static bound and a runtime break off a lever, which is exactly the plates' own `for(o=0;o<12;o++){ if(o>=octs) break; ... }` idiom. It accumulates ONE float and carries nothing else.
the_vocabulary_that_exists.descend(grid2(...), levels, {child, keep: a hierarchical subdivision walk. Carries a cell, a scale and an address hash, but its shape is fixed - the child arrow must be `(a) => a.child(ex, ey)` and a keep predicate decides survival.

what_is_missing.construct: a bounded loop that carries arbitrary state across iterations
what_is_missing.why: Twelve of the fourteen advect or accumulate something that is not a float and not a subdivision address: a vec2 trail, a vec3 point, a rolling hash, a running anisotropy. `sum` cannot express them because it accumulates one float; `descend` cannot because its body shape is fixed.
what_is_missing.shape_it_would_need: the same static-bound-plus-runtime-break emission sum() already does, generalised to a tuple of carried values, each bound to a `precise` local per iteration so nothing in the loop body becomes a contraction candidate.
what_is_missing.note: This is the single change that would take the emitted corpus from 54 to 66. It is also the change that would let `cascade` be emitted, which matters because cascade is the one plate that still splits across cards AND has no positive - every other splitter either has one already or was fixed by getting one.

throughput.note: loop-free but large; the port is long rather than blocked.

billiards.carries: a reflecting point and its direction

breakdown.carries: a walking point and a rolling hash

cascade.carries: a vec2 trail, a rolling hash, and a running height through nested step-by-octave advection
cascade.priority: HIGHEST - the only plate that both still splits across cards and has no positive

dissipation.carries: a cell, a scale, an address hash, a log-weight and an anisotropy - close to descend's shape but with no keep predicate and a hashed child rather than a chosen one

drainage.carries: a descending point and a rolling hash

rulespace.carries: a cellular automaton row and a rule index

tangle.carries: a vec3 point through a harmonic sum

how_this_was_measured: darkroom/spec.py load_plates(), then counting for-loops in each plate's `glsl` and reading what each loop body assigns back into a variable declared outside it. A loop whose only carried value is a float accumulator would be expressible as sum(); none of the twelve is.
